reasoning: The two groups address different gaps, so all nine edits are kept and nothing touches the protected section. There is no direct conflict. The failure group's edits (archive-answer handling, bare place names, echo-passage trap, grammatical form, pointer check, definition clues) are carried over unchanged. The success group's edits are kept because the failure group does not cover them. These are the media-cue handling, the two-way nickname rule and the brand/title guard for the delete-clue-words test. The brand/title guard is compatible with the failure group's bare-place-name rule, since type words like 'River' are separate category labels while brand words belong to the official name. Two insertions share an anchor: the definition-clue edit (failure) and the media-cue edit (success) both go after the Conch sentence. The place-name edit (failure) and the brand edit (success) both go after the 'hasty pudding' sentence. Both pairs cover different topics and can sit side by side, and the failure edit is listed first in each pair.

edits.target: Before the answer tags, briefly quote the matched line.
edits.content:
- Copy the archived answer IN FULL, including a qualifier that belongs to it and is not already stated in the clue. If the line reads 'It's the largest city in its state; ... | Anchorage, Alaska.', the answer is 'Anchorage, Alaska', not the trimmed 'Anchorage'. Do not apply the general name-shortening rules of Rule 4 to a verbatim archive answer.
- Copying does NOT exempt the answer from the Rule 4 delete-clue-words test. If the archived answer ends with the noun the clue's own 'this <noun>' already gives ('this market' + 'BEAR MARKET' -> 'Bear'), or adds a word that only repeats a clue word or its synonym ('giant snake' + 'Rainbow Serpent' -> 'Rainbow'), drop that echoed word. Keep the head noun only when the bare modifier alone would not name the entity ('Roman Empire').
- Archive dumps and flashcard pages often run clue and answer together with no separator ('...ARCHING ITS BODY Rainbow This "platinum-dome" character...', '...PRICE DROPS, BEAR MARKET.'). The answer is the short run of words right after the clue's last words and before the next clue.

edits.target: The 'do not repeat clue words' rule is for a separate modifier already stated in the clue ('hasty' + pudding).
edits.content: - Rivers, lakes, mountains, islands, cities and countries: give the bare proper name even when the passages add a type word. 'Amazon' (not 'Amazon River'), 'Nile', 'Roanoke'. If the pointer names a place type ('the 1945 conference in this Crimean city'), the slot is the PLACE ('Yalta'), never the event held there ('Yalta Conference'). Keep a type word only when it is an inseparable part of the name ('Lake Erie', 'Mount Everest', 'Great Salt Lake').

edits.target: Do not choose one that fits only some.
edits.content: - Echo-passage trap: a passage that repeats the clue with the blank filled ('Steller's Sea Cow was a relative of the dugong') is not proof by itself. Check the filler against EVERY descriptor the clue attaches to the slot ('this rare aquatic mammal found in Florida'). The dugong lives in the Indo-Pacific, so it fails and the manatee fits. If the filler fails any descriptor, answer the candidate that satisfies all of them. The descriptors after 'this' decide the answer, not the most-repeated word.

edits.target: - Put only the bare answer in the answer tags. Do not write a sentence, restate the clue, or add dates, qualifiers or alternatives. Brief reasoning belongs before the tags.
edits.content: - Match the grammatical form the clue's wording requires. 'This is the term for nonconductors like plastics' has a singular 'this' with plural examples, so the answer is the singular headword ('insulator', not 'insulators'). Plural examples inside the clue do not make the answer plural. If the clue defines the term with an -ing phrase ('this term for following a winding & turning course'), answer in the -ing form ('Meandering', not the base verb 'meander'). Write the form without an article.

edits.target: - Ask: what category is the answer (country, person, vitamin, object, band), and what member of that category fits all the clue details?
edits.content: - POINTER CHECK: before choosing among passage words, decide what TYPE the pointer asks for. (a) A bare pronoun clue ('he/she/his/her', no 'this') asks for the PERSON. Works, pictures, films or places named in the clue are anchors, and so are the 'more famous' neighbours it mentions. 'In the early 1500s, between 2 more famous pictures, he worked on his "Virgin and Child with St. Anne"' -> the artist (Leonardo da Vinci), not 'The Last Supper'. (b) 'this way / this manner / this often / this much' asks for the adverb or manner word that the joke or saying fills in. 'Play country music this way and your wife, dog & car return' -> 'backwards'. Things listed in the punchline or in passage variants ('prison', 'house') are not the answer. Take the word that follows the same verb phrase in the passages ('play a country song backwards'). (c) 'this phenomenon / this thing seen in the sky' asks for the bare thing itself ('Rainbow'), not a myth creature or title linked to it.

edits.target: and answer with the common English name (Conch).
edits.content: - Telegraphic definition clues with no pointer ('An astringent applied under the arms to curtail sweating') describe a CLASS of thing. The answer is the general product or thing-type that does exactly that, the headword the passages keep pairing with the action ('antiperspirant'). Do not answer with one ingredient, remedy or example that the passages list as a way to do it ('witch hazel', 'apple cider vinegar', 'tea tree oil'), and do not reuse the clue's own descriptor word ('astringent'). Test: all the listed examples should be members of your candidate, and your candidate should not be a member of them.

edits.target: and answer with the common English name (Conch).
edits.content: - Media cues ('seen here', 'shown here', 'heard here', 'pictured', 'whose structure is seen here') point to an image, video or audio clue you cannot perceive. Do not answer 'cannot tell' and do not guess from the missing picture. Drop the cue and resolve the clue from the textual hooks that remain: the function or use ('used as a bleach'), the class ('molecule', 'substance') and any named anchor. Choose the single entity that those hooks and the passage titles and snippets repeatedly tie together ('Hydrogen peroxide' for a 'simple molecule used as a bleach'). Give its standard full name without the category words the clue supplies. If passages are noisy, use your own knowledge to pick the well-known entity that fits every remaining hook.

edits.target: - For nickname clues about a person ('known as "Uncle Walter"'), answer with the real name as it appears in the context (Walter Cronkite), not the nickname. Still apply the person-name rule above.
edits.content: - Nickname clues about a person work in BOTH directions, so check which one is given. If the clue gives the nickname ('known as "Uncle Walter"'), answer with the real name as it appears in the context (Walter Cronkite), not the nickname. If the clue gives the real name and asks for the 'better known moniker / nickname / alias / stage name' ('William Marcy Tweed's better known moniker'), answer with the nickname alone ('Boss'), not the real name and not the nickname plus surname ('Boss Tweed'). Still apply the person-name rule above.

edits.target: The 'do not repeat clue words' rule is for a separate modifier already stated in the clue ('hasty' + pudding).
edits.content: - Brand, company and title names keep every word of their official form even when the clue echoes one of those words. 'If you need a hammer, this is "The Place With the Helpful Hardware Folks"' -> 'Ace Hardware' (bare 'Ace' is incomplete; the passages repeat 'Ace Hardware'). 'this nursery rhyme' -> 'Mary Had a Little Lamb' (drop only the category label 'nursery rhyme', not words inside the title). The delete-clue-words test removes separate category labels and modifiers, not words that belong to the proper name.
